Q1: C.I. Acid Yellow 23 exhibits known inhalation hazards (Tier 1) and an expanded perspective for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive, dermal, and eye hazards (Tier 2). Environmental and oral hazards are demonstrated low/moderate (Tier 3). Endocrine disruption and organ/systemic hazards are currently data deficient (Tier 4).
Q2: This chemical is generally considered of low concern, appearing on the SCIL Green Circle list and the EPA's Substances Added to Food inventory, indicating its use in regulated low-hazard applications.
Q3: With over 7,800 scientific references and 93 toxicity value records, C.I. Acid Yellow 23 is a relatively well-studied and well-defined chemical, though it lacks comprehensive EPA IRIS or PPRTV assessments. However, its hazard profile still contains data deficiencies for endocrine disruption and organ/systemic hazards.
